title: Valentine's Day on a Budget: The Real Cost of One Nice Dinner

lines.say: Valentine's Day. One nice dinner. How much could it cost?
Let's add up the real number, then build a version that fits your plan.
Here's the dinner.
Two entrées, seventy-six.
Appetizer and dessert, thirty.
Four drinks, forty-eight.
Tax, twelve.
And a twenty percent tip, thirty-one.

scene.label: Just the dinner
scene.sub: before flowers, a gift, or getting there

lines.say: That's one ninety-seven, before anything else.

lines.cap: Add flowers, $65. A gift, $75. And rides there and back, $30.
lines.say: Add flowers, sixty-five. A gift, seventy-five. And rides there and back, thirty.

lines.cap: In our example budget, fun money is $100 a paycheck. That one night is almost four paychecks of it.
lines.say: In our example budget, fun money is a hundred dollars a paycheck. That one night is almost four paychecks of it.
So here are two ways to do it without wrecking February.
Option one. The planned night in.
Here's a hundred dollar version.

lines.cap: Groceries for a really nice dinner, $48.
lines.say: Groceries for a really nice dinner, forty-eight.
A bottle of wine, eighteen.
Grocery-store flowers, fifteen.
Dessert to share, twelve.

lines.cap: And a printed photo with a handwritten card, $7. Often the part people remember most.
lines.say: And a printed photo with a handwritten card, seven. Often the part people remember most.

lines.cap: $100. One paycheck of fun money. $267 less than the night out.
lines.say: One hundred dollars. One paycheck of fun money. Two sixty-seven less than the night out.
Option two. Splurge on purpose.

lines.cap: The night out isn't wrong. Unplanned is the problem. If you love it, plan for it: $367 over 26 paychecks is $15 each.
lines.say: The night out isn't wrong. Unplanned is the problem. If you love it, plan for it. Three sixty-seven over twenty-six paychecks is fifteen dollars each.
Start a sinking fund now, and next February is already paid for. Episode three shows how.

scene.text: Decide the number before you sit down.

lines.say: Either way, decide the number before you're sitting at the table.
